A **skill** is reusable operating guidance for a kind of work. It tells an agent when a workflow applies, how to combine Consuelo tools, what boundaries to preserve, and how to verify the result.

A skill is different from a tool:

- **tools** perform typed operations;
- **skills** teach an agent how to combine operations well;
- **scripts** contain executable implementation when a workflow needs it.

Browse the skills that ship with OS in [Skill Templates](/build/skills/bundled/).

## The skill contract

A bundled skill normally starts with:

```text
skills/<name>/
  SKILL.md
  skill.json
```

`SKILL.md` is the guidance entrypoint. `skill.json` supplies compact discovery and policy metadata such as the skill name, trigger, permission, approval requirements, capabilities, and load path.

The generated catalog intentionally does **not** embed every `SKILL.md` body into steering. Steering advertises a compact active-skill list; the detailed guidance is loaded when the skill applies.

## Selection and installation

The durable selection lives in:

```text
<CONSUELO_HOME>/config.json
  selectedSkills: [...]
```

Consuelo reconciles that desired set into:

```text
<CONSUELO_HOME>/components/installed-skills.json
```

That active index is the preferred source for the Installed skills section of steering. Selected skill templates are also materialized in the visible user tree:

```text
~/Consuelo/Skills/<name>/
```

The full bundled catalog is visible at:

```text
~/Consuelo/Skills/skills.json
```

The immutable runtime implementation lives under `<CONSUELO_HOME>/runtime/current/skills/`.

## Enable and remove skills

Use the picker:

```bash
consuelo add skill
consuelo remove skill
```

Or name skills directly:

```bash
consuelo add skill branch browser
consuelo remove skill teach
```

Removing a clean managed skill removes its visible materialization. If the managed copy has local modifications, Consuelo deselects it but preserves the edited files for explicit review instead of deleting them.

## Disabled is different from unselected

`selectedSkills` controls installation. `manifest.overlay.json` can separately disable an installed skill from the effective runtime surface. Steering filters disabled skills even when they remain selected on disk.

## Legacy custom skills

Existing user-owned skills in the legacy hidden `<CONSUELO_HOME>/skills/` tree are preserved and represented as `legacyCustom` in the managed index for explicit migration. New bundled selection uses the current managed/visible layout above.
